_comment: SEEDED by `wowkb.capart import scenarios retribution` from projects/combat-assist/specs/retribution/scenarios.md, then reviewed by eye. The DOC leads: `capart check` re-scrapes the CDM-row bullets and fails if they disagree with this file. Edit the doc, re-import, review.

scenarios.title: Opener, everything ready, HP 0
scenarios.state: Pull timer at zero, every cooldown up, Holy Power 0, single-target mode, no procs. Holy Flames talented, Expurgation not yet on the target — the state the opener exists to end.

steps.html: ⚠ This scenario is read by pass 1, not by elimination — the only one in the catalog that is.
Blade of Justice wears priority (cue H, boj_opener) → press. generators 2, the rung that puts Expurgation up. The condition is that rung: Holy Flames talented, the DoT absent, the button ready.

Everything else is read only if the eye goes looking. Execution Sentence and Avenging Wrath are genuinely held — es_awaits_wrath_ready and aw_awaits_expurgation — and the two spenders are unaffordable at 0 Holy Power. None of that has to be interpreted to find the press.

extras.label: Eye-direction
extras.html: ⚠ This is the catalog's worked example of the density rule. Said by elimination, the opener needs four holds — Execution Sentence, Avenging Wrath, Wake of Ashes and Divine Toll all standing down so a left-to-right scan can reach position 7. That is over budget (../render-shelf.md Part 0.5) and it reads as "something is wrong" rather than "press the clean one". Promoting the press costs one badge and says the same thing. Two markers were deleted outright when this was authored — woa_awaits_wrath_ready and dt_awaits_wrath_ready — because they existed for no reason other than steering the scan past their own rows. That is the test of a promotion worth making: it should remove authored vocabulary, not add to it.

extras.label: Cue set
extras.html: Priority (H) → have. Readable hold (C) → have, on rows 1 and 2. Affordability (A) → have.

scenarios.title: HP 5, Wake of Ashes on cooldown — the interleave, resolved
scenarios.state: Single target, no procs, Holy Power 5. Execution Sentence, Avenging Wrath and Wake of Ashes are all on cooldown. Divine Toll is ready.

steps.html: Execution Sentence … Wake of Ashes — on cooldown → skip.
Divine Toll — available, and the overcap badge lights on the exact readable predicate resource >= 5: pressing it here throws away its whole Holy Power injection → skip.
Final Verdict — affordable, nothing rules it out → press. finishers 4, reached through the early finishers call at generators 1.

extras.label: Eye-direction
extras.html: ⚠ This is the scenario the whole row order is built for. finishers is called from inside generators, so the spenders outrank Divine Toll only at 5 Holy Power — a thing a fixed row order cannot say. One badge on one row says it instead, and it is readable, not sealed, because Holy Power is NeverSecret.

extras.label: Cue set
extras.html: Overcap (B) → have, and readable — the difference from Havoc, whose equivalent is a sealed Fury readout.

scenarios.title: HP 5, Wake of Ashes READY — and deliberately unbadged
scenarios.state: As RET-2, but Wake of Ashes is ready. Holy Power is still 5.

steps.html: Execution Sentence / Avenging Wrath — on cooldown → skip.
Wake of Ashes — available, carries no overcap badge by design, and neither sealed band is in range → press. generators 3.
Divine Toll — still badged; it never gets the chance to compete.

extras.label: Eye-direction
extras.html: ⚠ The badge that would be honest about generation would be wrong about the press. The APL's early finishers call is gated on cooldown.wake_of_ashes.remains — Wake of Ashes on cooldown — so at 5 Holy Power with it ready the APL presses it and accepts the waste, because what the button is worth is the Hammer of Light window. overcap is worn by exactly one row in this catalog, and this is the row it is kept off.

extras.label: Cue set
extras.html: Nothing fires. The press is pure elimination.

scenarios.title: Hammer of Light window open, HP 4
scenarios.state: Wake of Ashes has been cast; row 3 is displaying Hammer of Light. Holy Power 4. Execution Sentence and Avenging Wrath are on cooldown.

steps.html: Execution Sentence / Avenging Wrath — on cooldown → skip.

Hammer of Light — row 3 reads identity == transformed, so band 1 gives it ROTATION instead of COOLDOWN; both of its sealed holds are gated off by that same identity term, and woa_starved is dark at 4 Holy Power → press. finishers 2.

extras.label: Eye-direction
extras.html: ⚠ **This row was the catalog's single point of failure until 2026-08-18. Had the Cooldown Manager kept swiping it for Wake of Ashes's own running cooldown, the walk would skip straight past the free press and land on Divine Toll or a spender. It does not — the swipe follows the displayed** spell (Open facts 1, and knowledge/addon-dev/cooldown-manager.md §3.1.1). The two-band identity design stands on that fact.

extras.label: Cue set
extras.html: Identity (R7) → have. Nothing else fires.

scenarios.title: Hammer of Light window open, HP 2 — the window you cannot afford
scenarios.state: As RET-4, but Holy Power 2. Divine Toll is ready and Avenging Wrath is far away.

steps.html: Execution Sentence / Avenging Wrath — on cooldown → skip.
Hammer of Light — available, but starved lights: affordable is read on the live id, which is Hammer of Light's 3 Holy Power, not Wake of Ashes's zero → skip.
Divine Toll — no overcap at 2 Holy Power, and dt_awaits_wrath's band is out of range → press. generators 4, and the Holy Power it injects is what re-arms the window.

extras.label: Eye-direction
extras.html: Affordability read on the live identity is what makes this row honest. Read on the base id it would be free, the badge would stay dark, and the walk would stop on a button the player cannot press.

extras.label: Cue set
extras.html: Affordability (A) on the live id (R1 + R7) → have.

scenarios.title: HP 4, Art of War proc — a free Blade of Justice outranks spending
scenarios.state: Single target, Art of War (or Righteous Cause) is up, Holy Power 4, every cooldown down, Blade of Justice ready.

steps.html: Execution Sentence … Divine Toll — on cooldown → skip.
Final Verdict — affordable, but blocked lights from tv_awaits_blade: a proc is up, Blade of Justice is ready, and Holy Power is ≤ 4 → skip.
Divine Storm — the same badge, from ds_awaits_blade → skip.
Blade of Justice — press. generators 5, which sits above generators 6.

extras.label: Eye-direction
extras.html: ⚠ This is why ds_awaits_blade exists as a second marker. Badging only row 5 would hand the walk to row 6 and the player would press Divine Storm — the correct answer to "not Templar's Verdict" and the wrong answer to the question actually being asked.

extras.label: Cue set
extras.html: Readable hold (D) → have, on both spenders. Both proc buffs are registered spell-activation overlays and both point at Blade of Justice 184575, so the APL's OR authors itself as one proc term.

scenarios.title: HP 5, Art of War proc — the proc loses

steps.html: Execution Sentence … Divine Toll — on cooldown → skip.
Final Verdict — row 5's proc-defer marker requires resource <= 4, which is false here, so the badge stays dark → press.

extras.label: Eye-direction
extras.html: The resource <= 4 term on the marker is doing the same job the overcap badge does in RET-2, from the other side: at 5 Holy Power the early finishers call outranks generators 5, so the proc'd Blade of Justice correctly loses to the spender sitting left of it.

extras.label: Cue set
extras.html: Nothing fires. Elimination, with a readable term keeping the badge off.

scenarios.title: AoE mode on, 4 targets, HP 4
scenarios.state: The player has flipped cap's AoE toggle; four targets, no Empyrean Legacy proc, Holy Power 4, cooldowns down.

steps.html: Execution Sentence … Divine Toll — on cooldown → skip.

Final Verdict — the st_only pawn from tv_divine_storm_aoe: the toggle is on, no Empyrean Legacy proc is live, and the spend is affordable → skip. ⚠ Not blocked — nothing is held here and nothing would be wasted, it is simply the other spender's turn.

Divine Storm — press. finishers 3, via ds_castable's target clause. - ⚠ The 2-vs-3 target threshold is the player's, not cap's. Tempest of the Lightbringer without Jurisdiction moves it, and cap models no enemy count — the toggle is the whole interface. This scenario says what the badge does once the toggle is on, not when to flip it.

extras.label: Cue set
extras.html: Mode (E) → have, gated on the aoe predicate. Its mirror aoe_only rides Divine Storm in single target, and the pair is what lets the two spenders be told apart at all.

scenarios.title: Single target, Empyrean Power proc, HP 4
scenarios.state: Single target, Empyrean Power is up, Holy Power 4, cooldowns down. The AoE toggle is off.

steps.html: Execution Sentence … Divine Toll — on cooldown → skip.

Final Verdict — blocked from tv_empyrean_power → skip. ⚠ blocked, not the st_only pawn RET-8 wears. The mode is right here; what rules Final Verdict out is a free Divine Storm waiting, which is precisely "a readable dependency says the press would be wasted". A pawn here would tell the player their mode was wrong when it was not.
Divine Storm — press. A free Divine Storm satisfies ds_castable with no target term at all, which is why this row looks identical to RET-8 and is a different marker.

extras.label: Eye-direction
extras.html: ⚠ This scenario and RET-8 used to look identical, and stopped on 2026-08-19. Both put a badge on Final Verdict, and while the vocabulary had one negative key for both, the argument here was that the player does not need to know which clause of ds_castable fired. That was a concession to the vocabulary rather than a finding: the two reasons are a mode and a proc, they are acted on differently — one is fixed by the toggle, the other passes on its own — and the badge's job is to carry the reason. Now they differ.

extras.label: Cue set
extras.html: Proc-defer (D) → have, gated on proc rather than on aoe.

scenarios.title: AoE mode on, Empyrean Legacy proc, HP 4 — the exception to the exception
scenarios.state: AoE toggle on, Empyrean Legacy is up, Holy Power 4.

steps.html: Execution Sentence … Divine Toll — on cooldown → skip.
Final Verdict — both E markers carry !proc(templars_verdict), which is now false, so row 5 is clear even in AoE → press.

extras.label: Eye-direction
extras.html: ⚠ **This state is why !proc(templars_verdict) is a term on both markers rather than a third marker of its own.** It is ds_castable's &!buff.empyrean_legacy.up clause: an empowered Templar's Verdict beats Divine Storm at four targets. Expressed as a separate rule it would have had to un-badge a row, and the marker grammar is AND-only — there is no un-badging, only a term that keeps the badge dark.

extras.label: Cue set
extras.html: Nothing fires; the negation is what keeps it that way.

scenarios.title: HP 2, no procs, Blade of Justice on cooldown
scenarios.state: Holy Power 2, no procs, every cooldown and Blade of Justice on cooldown.

steps.html: Execution Sentence … Divine Toll — on cooldown → skip.
Final Verdict / Divine Storm — available and starved: 2 Holy Power will not pay for a 3-cost spend → skip.
Blade of Justice — on cooldown → skip.
Judgment — press. generators 10 — or Hammer of Wrath (generators 9), if that is what row 8 is currently displaying; the row is one button and the client picks which.

extras.label: Eye-direction
extras.html: The generator is reached by subtraction, exactly as Havoc's Felblade is: nothing promotes it, the two spenders above it demote themselves.

extras.label: Cue set
extras.html: Affordability (A) → have.

scenarios.title: Execution Sentence ready, Avenging Wrath ~10s out, HP 2
scenarios.state: Execution Sentence is up. Avenging Wrath is ~10s from ready, Wake of Ashes is far away, Divine Toll is up, Holy Power 2, Blade of Justice ready.

steps.html: Execution Sentence — available, and blocked lights from two markers at once (es_awaits_wrath at within = 15, es_awaits_wake at beyond = 1.5). One badge, because naming the same cue twice unions into one badge — and that union is the OR → skip.
Avenging Wrath / Wake of Ashes — on cooldown → skip.
Divine Toll — blocked from dt_awaits_wrath, the same 15s band → skip.
Final Verdict / Divine Storm — starved at 2 Holy Power → skip.
Blade of Justice — press. generators 8.

extras.label: Eye-direction
extras.html: Hold Execution Sentence: Avenging Wrath is close and Wake of Ashes is not, so the placed cooldown is worth a few seconds of patience. Divine Toll is held for the same window. ⚠ Both are sealed — cap hands over a band and never learns where inside it the value fell, so this is confirmed by eye in game, not by a capture.

extras.label: Cue set
extras.html: Sealed hold (C) → sealed, on rows 1 and 4. Affordability (A) → have.

scenarios.title: Execution Sentence, Avenging Wrath and Wake of Ashes all ready, HP 3
scenarios.state: The state the sealed band cannot cover: Avenging Wrath is ready, i.e. zero remaining. Execution Sentence and Wake of Ashes are up too. Holy Power 3. Mid-fight, so Expurgation is ticking and aw_awaits_expurgation is dark — the difference from RET-1.

steps.html: Execution Sentence — blocked from es_awaits_wrath_ready, the readable half of the hold: cooldown.avenging_wrath.remains>15 is false at zero → skip.
Avenging Wrath — press.

extras.label: Eye-direction
extras.html: ⚠ A sealed band deliberately reads nothing at zero remaining, so RET-12's band goes dark in exactly the state where the hold matters most. Row 1 is the only row in this catalog carrying a readable companion to a sealed hold, and the reason is position: it sits left of everything it waits on, so a quiet row 1 would be pressed before the eye ever reached Avenging Wrath. Rows sitting to the right of what they wait on need only the band — elimination covers their zero case. Position in the row decides which halves a hold needs. ⚠ RET-1 tested that rule and it held, but only just. There, cue G holds a ready Avenging Wrath, so the walk does not stop at row 2 and rows 3 and 4 briefly needed companions of their own. Promoting the opener (cue H) removed the need and both were deleted. The rule survives because a promoted scenario is never read by elimination at all.

extras.label: Cue set
extras.html: Readable hold (C) → have, the counter to RET-12's sealed one. What the walk did not have to explain. No state in it required cap to know a target count, a buff duration, or which of two Hammer of Light states was live. Every skip above is a readable Lua term, a sealed band on a cooldown, or — at RET-1 only — the readable up/down latch on a target aura that cues G and H are both built from. One scenario in thirteen is read by pass 1. RET-1 is the catalog's only promotion, and the ratio is the point: a vocabulary where the positive cue is reached often has stopped being a reading model and become a pointer (../render-shelf.md Part 0.5). ⚠ Row 9 renders only on a Templar Strikes build. Crusader Strike binds nothing otherwise, so on any other build the row simply is not there and the walk is eight entries wide. It is drawn in every scenario above because a row that exists on some build has to be shown reaching the end of the walk somewhere.
